{{Color box|{{party color|Asenso Manileño}}|border=darkgray}} [[Asenso Manileño]] | blank2_name = Congressional bloc | blank2_info = Majority }} '''Manila's 2nd congressional district''' is one of the six [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the city of [[Manila]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 20, 2020}} The district consists of [[barangay]]s 147 to 267 in the eastern part of the Manila district of [[Tondo, Manila|Tondo]] (also known as Gagalangin), east of Dagupan Street, Estero de Vitas and Estero de Sunog Apog bordering [[Navotas]] and southern [[Caloocan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=April 10, 2020}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Rolan Valeriano|Rolando M. Valeriano]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP) and [[Asenso Manileño]].{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 20, 2020}} Prior to the revision of Manila's city charter in 1949, it consisted of the southern and eastern Manila districts of [[Ermita]], [[Malate, Manila|Malate]], [[Paco, Manila|Paco]], [[Pandacan]], [[Quiapo, Manila|Quiapo]], [[Sampaloc, Manila|Sampaloc]] (including the present-day [[Santa Mesa]]), [[San Miguel, Manila|San Miguel]], [[Santa Ana, Manila|Santa Ana]] (including the present-day [[San Andres, Manila|San Andres]]), and [[Santa Cruz, Manila|Santa Cruz]]. Following the revision and until its second dissolution in 1972, it retained Quiapo and Santa Cruz while [[Binondo]] and [[San Nicolas, Manila|San Nicolas]] were added to its jurisdiction.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=409|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1949/06/18/republic-act-no-409/ |title=An act to revise the charter of the City of Manila, and for other purposes|date=June 18, 1949 |accessdate=October 27, 2023|publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)|Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines]]}} After the restoration of the Congress in 1987, it encompassed the eastern part of Tondo, which remains the case to the present. ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Legislature ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
